data.name: Study Intervention Dosing Interval (once weekly SC)
Exclusionary Antihyperglycemic Medication Washout (amylin analogs, GLP-1 RA, GIP/GLP RA, insulin)
Insulin Therapy Prohibition Prior to Visit 1
Baseline Fundus Photography Prior to Randomization
Cardiovascular Event Lookback (e.g., acute myocardial infarction)
Chronic Systemic Glucocorticoid Lookback (>2 weeks duration)
Stable Dose Requirement for Weight-Gain-Causing Medications
Prohibited Duration of On-Study Insulin Use
Randomization Eligibility at Visit 3
data.description: Participant must complete screening (Visit 1 to Visit 3, up to 35 days) and meet all eligibility criteria including baseline fundus photography and PHQ-9 assessment prior to randomization at Visit 3
data.text: All participants will have a baseline fundus photography assessment prior to randomization (Visit 3). Qualifying fundus photographs obtained within 90 days before Visit 1 may be used for eligibility determination.

data.name: PHQ-9 Exclusionary Threshold
data.description: Depression severity threshold assessed at screening and randomization
data.text: Have a PHQ-9 score of 15 or more at any screening visit (Visit 1) or at randomization (Visit 3).

data.name: Fasting Glucose Threshold at Screening
data.description: Central laboratory confirmed hyperglycemia threshold excluding participation
data.text: Have fasting glucose >270 mg/dL (>15.0 mmol/L) confirmed by the central laboratory at screening (Visit 1).

data.name: Renal Function Threshold at Screening
data.description: eGFR threshold determined by central laboratory during screening
data.text: Have renal impairment measured as eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2, calculated by eGFRcr-cys formula as per Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration as determined by central laboratory during screening (Visit 1).

data.name: Severe, Persistent Hyperglycemia Requiring Rescue
data.description: Condition triggering glycemic rescue therapy during the treatment period
data.text: Rescue Therapy for Severe, Persistent Hyperglycemia: participants must continue administering assigned study intervention unless insulin is used as short-term rescue therapy. Urgent use of short-term insulin in a hospital or closely monitored setting may be used as rescue therapy.

data.name: Prohibited On-Study Insulin Duration
data.description: Limit on consecutive days of insulin use during the study
data.text: Insulin use for ≥14 consecutive days is prohibited.

data.name: Liver Chemistry Stopping Criteria
data.description: Hepatic safety monitoring criteria for study drug interruption or discontinuation
data.text: Liver chemistry stopping criteria (Section 7.1.1 and Section 8.2.9) define criteria for study drug interruption or permanent discontinuation.

data.name: Low BMI Threshold for Dose Modification
data.description: Management of participants reaching low BMI during treatment
data.text: Management of Participants with BMI ≤22 kg/m2 (Section 6.6.3).

data.name: Perceived Excessive Weight Reduction
data.description: Condition prompting dose modification per Section 6.6.4
data.text: Management of Participants with Perceived Excessive Weight Reduction (Section 6.6.4).

data.name: Intestinal Symptoms / Inadequate Nutrition or Dehydration
data.description: Gastrointestinal tolerability conditions prompting dose modification
data.text: Management of Participants with Intestinal Symptoms (Section 6.6.1) and Management of Participants with Inadequate Nutrition or Dehydration (Section 6.6.2).

data.name: Enrollment Cap by Sex Assigned at Birth
data.description: Enrollment condition to ensure adequate representation
data.text: An upper limit of approximately 70% enrollment of AFAB participants will be used to ensure a sufficient number of AMAB participants.

data.name: Randomization Allocation Condition
data.description: Approximately 1035 participants randomized to placebo, eloralintide 1.5 mg, 3 mg, 6 mg, 9 mg at 2:1:2:2:2 ratio
data.text: Approximately 1035 participants will be randomly assigned to treatment arms of placebo, eloralintide 1.5 mg, eloralintide 3 mg, eloralintide 6 mg, and eloralintide 9 mg at a randomization ratio of 2:1:2:2:2.

data.name: Unscheduled Visit Condition
data.description: Investigator-discretion visit for clinical oversight
data.text: An unscheduled visit may occur per investigator discretion for clinical oversight. The study site will determine if fasting status is needed prior to the visit. Concomitant medications, AEs, and endpoint events are required and should be recorded in the CRF.

data.name: ED Procedure Exemption
data.description: Participants withdrawing before any dose do not require ED procedures
data.text: Participants who withdraw from the study after signing the informed consent but who have not taken a dose of study intervention do not need to complete ED procedures.

data.name: Screening to Treatment Transition
data.text: After an up to 35-day screening period (Visit 1 to Visit 3), participants meeting all eligibility criteria (including fasting glucose ≤270 mg/dL, eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m2, PHQ-9 <15 at Visit 1 and Visit 3, and baseline fundus photography) are randomized at Visit 3 to placebo or eloralintide 1.5, 3, 6, or 9 mg SC QW (2:1:2:2:2).

data.name: Dose Escalation to Treatment Maintenance Transition
data.text: After the 12-week dose escalation period (stepping through 3 mg, 6 mg, and 9 mg every 4 weeks), participants enter the 52-week treatment maintenance period at their randomly assigned final dose.

data.name: Treatment to Post-treatment Follow-up Transition
data.text: Following the last treatment period visit or final treatment visit (maximum treatment duration 64 weeks), all participants enter a 6-week posttreatment follow-up period and are required to complete the safety follow-up visit (Visit 801) approximately 6 weeks after the last treatment visit.

data.name: Dose Escalation Step
data.text: To reach the doses of 3 mg, 6 mg, and 9 mg QW, a dose-escalation regimen stepping through each of these doses every 4 weeks will be employed.

data.name: Dose Modification for Intestinal Symptoms
data.text: Dose modification per Section 6.6.1 for management of participants with intestinal symptoms.

data.name: Dose Modification for Inadequate Nutrition or Dehydration
data.text: Dose modification per Section 6.6.2 for management of participants with inadequate nutrition or dehydration.

data.name: Dose Modification for BMI ≤22 kg/m2
data.text: Dose modification per Section 6.6.3 for management of participants with BMI ≤22 kg/m2.

data.name: Dose Modification for Perceived Excessive Weight Reduction
data.text: Dose modification per Section 6.6.4 for management of participants with perceived excessive weight reduction.

data.name: Rescue Therapy for Severe, Persistent Hyperglycemia
data.text: Participants must continue administering assigned study intervention, unless insulin is used as short-term rescue therapy. Urgent use of short-term insulin in a hospital or closely monitored setting may be used as rescue therapy for severe, persistent hyperglycemia. Insulin use for ≥14 consecutive days is prohibited.

data.name: Temporary Study Intervention Interruption
data.text: Temporary study intervention interruption per Section 7.1.2, including interruption triggered by hepatic safety monitoring criteria (Section 8.2.9).

data.name: Discontinuation of Study Intervention for Liver Chemistry
data.text: Liver chemistry stopping criteria (Section 7.1.1) require permanent discontinuation of study intervention; hepatic safety monitoring and evaluation criteria for study drug interruption or discontinuation are described in Section 8.2.9.

data.name: Discontinuation of Study Intervention
data.text: Discontinuation of study intervention per Section 7.1; participants permanently discontinuing study intervention should complete early discontinuation (ED) visit procedures and posttreatment follow-up visit(s).

data.name: Participant Withdrawal from Study
data.text: Participant discontinuation/withdrawal from the study per Section 7.2. If the participant is discontinuing at the time of a scheduled visit, perform that visit as an ED visit.

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED) Visit
data.description: ED visits will be completed by participants permanently discontinuing early from the study. These participants should also complete posttreatment follow-up visit(s). If the participant is discontinuing at the time of a scheduled visit, that visit is performed as an ED visit.

data.name: Withdrawal Prior to First Dose
data.description: Participants who withdraw from the study after signing the informed consent but who have not taken a dose of study intervention do not need to complete ED procedures.

data.name: Screen Failure
data.description: Participants not meeting eligibility criteria during the up-to-35-day screening period (Visit 1 to Visit 3) exit prior to randomization (e.g., fasting glucose >270 mg/dL, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2, PHQ-9 ≥15 at Visit 1 or Visit 3).

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: Participant lost to follow up per Section 7.3.

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of up to 64 weeks of treatment (12-week dose escalation plus 52-week maintenance) followed by the 6-week posttreatment follow-up period, including the required safety follow-up visit (Visit 801) approximately 6 weeks after the last treatment visit.

data.name: Randomization Eligibility Decision
data.description: At Visit 3 (end of up to 35-day screening), eligibility is confirmed and participants are randomized 2:1:2:2:2 to placebo or eloralintide 1.5, 3, 6, or 9 mg SC QW.

data.name: Dose Escalation Step Decision (every 4 weeks)
data.description: During the 12-week dose escalation period, dose is stepped up every 4 weeks toward the assigned final dose, subject to tolerability and dose modification criteria.

data.name: Glycemic Rescue Decision
data.description: At treatment visits (every 4 to 12 weeks), investigator assesses severe, persistent hyperglycemia and may initiate short-term insulin rescue therapy in a hospital or closely monitored setting; insulin use for ≥14 consecutive days is prohibited.

data.name: Hepatic Safety Interruption/Discontinuation Decision
data.description: Hepatic safety monitoring at scheduled and unscheduled visits determines temporary interruption or permanent discontinuation of study intervention.

data.name: End of Treatment Transition Decision
data.description: At completion of the maximum 64-week treatment duration, participants transition to the 6-week posttreatment follow-up period and Visit 801.
